title: 12 Week FULL Mobility System
goal:
This system restores posterior chain length, control, and movement confidence through two complementary tracks:
Track A: Posterior Chain Eccentric Protocol
Track B: Mobility Conditioning Circuit
The program is designed to be repeatable, progressive, and durable, not a short-term mobility fix.
Most days use one track only.
One day per week, both tracks are intentionally combined.

principles.title: POSTERIOR CHAIN TRACK — LOADING & DEPTH INTENT
principles.text:
External load in the Posterior Chain Track is used as a tool to access deeper range of motion under control, not to chase intensity.
Depth always earns load. Load never forces depth.

overview.focus: PHASE 1 — RESET & DECOMPRESS. GOAL: Reduce protective tension and improve positioning.
PHASE 2 — RE-LENGTHEN & ACTIVATE. GOAL: Create usable mobility.
PHASE 3 — GROUND MOBILITY DEVELOPMENT. GOAL: Own new ranges of motion.
PHASE 4 — ROTATION & STABILITY. GOAL: Build rotational control and trunk stability.
PHASE 5 — DYNAMIC MOBILITY. GOAL: Transfer mobility into movement.
PHASE 6 — PERFORMANCE MOBILITY. GOAL: Maintain mobility under athletic conditions.

guidelines: HOW THE BALANCE SHIFTS — Weeks 1-2 lean toward mobility: Track B (mobility circuit) 3x/week, Track A (posterior chain strength) 2x/week. From Week 3 the balance shifts toward strength: Track A 3x/week, Track B 2x/week, through Week 12.
TRACK A PROGRESSION ROADMAP — WEEKS 1-4 FOUNDATION: Minimal load. Learn positions and master eccentric control.
TRACK A PROGRESSION ROADMAP — WEEKS 5-8 BUILD: Increase load 10-20% while maintaining perfect control and positions.
TRACK A PROGRESSION ROADMAP — WEEKS 9-12 ADVANCE: Continue to progress load. Maintain perfect eccentric control and full range.

WEEKS 1-2: EXPLORATORY DEPTH UNDER CONTROL — Load: Minimal. Focus: Gradual, self-regulated increase in depth. Each repetition may move slightly deeper than the previous repetition, only if: Control is maintained; Breathing remains calm; No guarding or compensation appears; Depth is never forced. Movement should feel light, smooth, and controlled, as if the load is guiding depth rather than pulling the body into it. If depth decreases or control is lost, the set is stopped or load is reduced immediately.

WEEKS 3-4: CONTROLLED DEPTH EXPANSION — Load: Moderate. Focus: Owning greater usable depth. Load may increase slightly to allow access to deeper positions while maintaining slow eccentrics, alignment, and consistency.
WEEKS 5-6: OWNED DEPTH — Load: Increased as tolerated. Focus: Stable, repeatable depth under full control. If added load reduces depth or control, load is reduced immediately.

TRACK COMBINATION RULE — Track A and Track B are typically performed on separate days. One day per week, both tracks are performed together. Combined Day Order: Track A first; Track B second, at a controlled pace. This day reinforces newly gained range through full-body movement.

OPTION 1 — WEEKS 1-2 OF THE PROGRAM (TRACK A TWICE PER WEEK). 3 TRACK B DAYS • 1 FULL REST DAY (OPTIONAL TRACK B ON SATURDAY). MON: TRACK A (Complete Track A Workout; Daily Checklist (Below)). TUE: TRACK B (Complete Track B Circuit; Daily Checklist (Below)). WED: TRACK B (Complete Track B Circuit; Daily Checklist (Below)). THU: TRACK A (Complete Track A Workout; Daily Checklist (Below)). FRI: TRACK B (Complete Track B Circuit; Daily Checklist (Below)). SAT: ACTIVE RECOVERY, OPTIONAL TRACK B (Active Recovery Checklist (Below) OR Track B Circuit). SUN: REST DAY (Full Rest Day; Daily Checklist (Below)). This option is for Weeks 1-2 to build the foundation. Track A = 2x/week, Track B = 3x/week.

OPTION 2 — WEEKS 3-12 OF THE PROGRAM (TRACK A THREE TIMES PER WEEK). 2 TRACK B DAYS • 1 ACTIVE RECOVERY DAY • 1 FULL REST DAY. MON: TRACK A (Complete Track A Workout; Daily Checklist (Below)). TUE: TRACK B (Complete Track B Circuit; Daily Checklist (Below)). WED: TRACK A (Complete Track A Workout; Daily Checklist (Below)). THU: ACTIVE RECOVERY (Active Recovery Checklist (Below); Optional Track B Circuit). FRI: TRACK B (Complete Track B Circuit; Daily Checklist (Below)). SAT: TRACK A (Complete Track A Workout; Daily Checklist (Below)). SUN: REST DAY (Full Rest Day; Daily Checklist (Below)). This option begins in Week 3 and continues through Week 12. Track A = 3x/week, Track B = 2x/week.
WALKING: Weeks 1-2: 20-30 MIN DAILY; Weeks 3-12: 25-30 MIN DAILY.

weeks.label: TRACK A — POSTERIOR CHAIN ECCENTRIC PROTOCOL
weeks.focus: THE GOAL: BUILD LENGTH, STRENGTH & RESILIENCE IN THE POSTERIOR CHAIN
weeks.notes:

VOLUME 3 SETS × 12-20 REPS
TEMPO 4-6 SECOND LOWERING PHASE

- Session Length: 25–35 minutes
- Prescription (All Movements): 3 sets × 12–20 reps, 4–6 second eccentric
- Concentric phase assisted or unloaded as needed

weeks.label: TRACK B — MOBILITY CONDITIONING CIRCUIT
weeks.notes:
- Frequency: 3× per week in Weeks 1-2, then 2× per week from Week 3
- Duration: 30 minutes
- Format: Continuous circuit, same order each round

Mobility Circuit (Fixed Order)

Goal:
- 5 full rounds in 30 minutes
- All movements unassisted
- No form breakdown or joint irritation

Complete rounds continuously for approximately 30 minutes (± 2-3 minutes). Do not count rounds. Simply continue cycling through the movements until approximately 30 minutes has elapsed.

uncertain: Structure is my mapping: the sources have no per-week sheets. 'track-a' and 'track-b' entries hold the two sessions that repeat all 12 weeks; the six 2-week 'weeks' entries come from the poster's 12-WEEK MOBILITY PROGRESSION ROADMAP, which lists movement names only (no sets/reps/how-to) and does not say when in the week they are done.

Load timelines differ between sources: rules doc gives weeks 1-2 / 3-4 / 5-6 (only six weeks), poster Track A roadmap gives 1-4 FOUNDATION / 5-8 BUILD / 9-12 ADVANCE. Both kept verbatim in progression.guidelines.

Track A frequency: rules doc and poster say 2-4x/week; weekly sheet fixes it at 2x (weeks 1-2) and 3x (weeks 3-12). Rules-doc example calendar (3x A, 2x B + combined Friday) differs from the weekly sheet's Option 1/Option 2.
Track B goal conflict: poster/rules doc 'GOAL: 5 ROUNDS IN 30 MINUTES' vs weekly sheet 'Do not count rounds ... approximately 30 minutes (± 2-3 minutes)'.
Bear Crawl distance: poster/weekly sheet 'x 4 LENGTHS' vs rules doc '~20 feet' (6-week PDF says '4 lengths of 20 ft').

Track A has 7 exercises on the poster and weekly checklist but 6 in the rules doc (Baseball Cable Swing missing from the doc). Track A dosage (3 × 12-20, 4-6 s lowering) applied to Baseball Cable Swing because the poster header states it for the protocol; the card itself says 'swing across body explosively'.
Typo kept as printed: Kneeling Straight Arm Cable Pulldown 'Lower up slowly for 4-6 seconds.'
Acupressure mat progression on Track B poster reads 'Week 4+:' — the '+' glyph is blurry (rendered like '4∘'); weekly sheet says 'WEEKS 4-12'. Poster 'Week 2-3' vs weekly sheet 'WEEKS 2-3'.

Exercise names: poster card titles are in ALL CAPS; written in the mixed case used on the weekly checklist sheet (1V4ILNrn9i9FOkgWmFKp-ruBx7PgrPLrp). Rules-doc names are kept in dosage.other['Rules doc heading'].

Extra (non-schema) field 'video' on Track A/B exercises: matched by video file name in the Track A / Track B movement folders; the calf-drop video is used for both calf exercises, HIP_THRUST for Glute Hip Bridge, BASEBALL_CABLE_STRETCH for Baseball Cable Swing, OVERHEAD_STRAIGHT_ARM_PULLDOWN for the kneeling pulldown — matching by name only, videos not watched.

Title: no single printed title for the whole system; used the File Links doc/folder name. Rules doc title is 'POSTERIOR CHAIN MOBILITY & LENGTH SYSTEM'; weekly sheet title is 'MD FIT WEEKLY PROGRAM & DAILY CHECKLIST'.

Dr. Jared's decision (Nov 2026): phases split differently in weeks 1-2 (more mobility) and then shift toward strength / balance. Track A/B frequencies set to Option 1 (wk 1-2) and Option 2 (wk 3-12); removed the rules-doc example calendar that conflicted: EXAMPLE WEEKLY CALENDAR — Monday: Track A — Posterior Chain Eccentric Protocol. Tuesday: Track B — Mobility Conditioning Circuit. Wednesday: Track A — Posterior Chain Eccentric Protocol. Thursday: Track B — Mobility Conditioning Circuit. Friday: Track A + Track B (Combined Day) Track A first, Track B second. Saturday: Optional Track A or Active Recovery. Sunday: Full Rest.
